decisions.title: Comparison-condition design
decisions.current_implementation: Selected three-condition development design: raw heterogeneous evidence only; neutral structured event table plus the same underlying evidence; Activity Receipt plus the same underlying evidence. Versioned implementation is required before the comparison-condition freeze gate is complete.

candidates.description: Control = heterogeneous evidence only; Receipt = same evidence plus standardized Activity Receipt.
Raw evidence, neutral structured event table plus raw evidence, and Receipt plus raw evidence, allowing separation of generic evidence organization from Receipt-specific presentation.

decisions.notes: The earlier two-condition repository draft and the 2026-09-15 research-review recommendation remain preserved as conflicting historical inputs. The owner explicitly selected three_condition_structured_control on 2026-09-20; two_condition_current remains listed but is not selected.
decisions.rationale: Selected explicitly by the project owner to separate benefit from generic evidence organization/structuring from any additional benefit attributable specifically to the Activity Receipt presentation/semantic layer. The three conditions are raw heterogeneous evidence only; a neutral structured event table plus the same underlying evidence; and Activity Receipt plus the same underlying evidence.

decisions.title: Primary confirmatory endpoint
decisions.current_implementation: Repository protocol reports prespecified component endpoints separately and explicitly has no post-hoc weighted composite primary score.

candidates.description: Prespecify a small primary set drawn from the existing action/source/incident F1 and categorical reconstruction endpoints, with timing reported separately.
Evidence-supported correct audit completion by 180 seconds: all required judgments correct with supported evidence and no fabricated material event/authorization; timeout cannot pass.

decisions.notes: The earlier research review proposed a single interpretable deadline-based primary endpoint; the current repository draft intentionally decomposes endpoints. A deliberate preregistration choice is still required.

decisions.title: Primary timing definition
decisions.current_implementation: Development runner records both wall and active elapsed time; page visibility automatically pauses active time and analysis requires an explicit active-vs-wall choice.

candidates.description: Use active time as primary timing measure, excluding explicit manual/visibility pause intervals under frozen rules.
Include elapsed background/hidden time in the primary deadline and prespecify sensitivity analysis for trials with more than 10 seconds hidden rather than silently pausing selected trials.

decisions.notes: Instrumentation already preserves both clocks, so this decision can be frozen later without losing development observability. Do not select timing after confirmatory outcomes are visible.

decisions.title: Misleading-Receipt robustness design
decisions.current_implementation: Current repository protocol includes stale, incomplete, and conflicting Receipt challenge strata alongside ordinary cases and requires separate reporting.

candidates.description: Include prespecified stale/incomplete/conflicting Receipt strata within the broader balanced assignment and report ordinary/challenge results separately.
Use a distinct misleading-Receipt experiment/cohort with raw, faithful-Receipt, and corrupted-Receipt presentations as proposed in the research review.

decisions.notes: Either architecture can preserve the robustness question, but the sampling/randomization implications differ materially and must be chosen before corpus/assignment freeze.

decisions.title: Target reviewer population and eligibility
decisions.current_implementation: Protocol requires experience bands, language proficiency, project-familiarity rules, and exclusion of case constructors/scorers, but no target population is frozen.

candidates.description: Select a reviewer population whose recruitment matches the intended scope of any human-audit claim; preserve explicit eligibility/exclusion criteria.

decisions.notes: A convenience sample must not be generalized to a professional population without justification.

decisions.title: Minimally meaningful effect or precision target
decisions.current_implementation: Independent-observation and crossed-design sensitivity tools exist, but their example effect/variance assumptions are explicitly illustrative.

candidates.description: Freeze a minimally meaningful condition effect or precision target before final crossed-design sample-size planning.

Use the project research review's proposed preregistration decision assumptions: +5 percentage points as the smallest practically important supported-completion benefit; 3 percentage points as the accuracy noninferiority margin for a separate speed claim; and +2 percentage points as the maximum acceptable increase in critical false clearance. These are candidate decision assumptions, not industry norms.

decisions.notes: The earlier research review supplies explicit candidate thresholds (+5pp benefit, 3pp speed-claim accuracy noninferiority margin, +2pp maximum critical-false-clearance increase) and asks that their acceptability be confirmed before confirmatory outcomes. The current repository planning examples remain illustrative. No threshold is selected by this ledger.
